notes: Cols 42-44 'Others' conclude Vernaculars of the Punjab (continued from p.268); cols 45-65 begin Other Indian Vernaculars (Total, Kashmiri, Sindhi, Gujarati, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu); the group continues on p.270. Print inconsistency: Kashmiri, Kangra (serial 7) printed persons 536, males 466, females 64 (466+64=530); Jullundur Division persons 2,627 agrees with 530, so the persons figure 536 is a misprint - kept as printed. Marathi Gujranwala males printed damaged (read 14, consistent with 29-15 and Lahore Division total); Tamil Ambala (serial 5) persons 28 has a damaged second digit (consistent with 26+2 and Ambala Division total 84). Cross-leaf check: Other Indian Vernaculars Total (cols 45-47) for Amritsar prints 7,141 persons / 3,008 females, one person (female) more than the sum of its language columns on leaves 0275-0276 (7,140/3,007); the excess carries into Lahore Division, British Territory and Punjab. The Asiatic Total on leaf 0277 is short by exactly one Amritsar female, so the print apparently counted one female under Other Indian Vernaculars in the totals but under Persian (or another Asiatic language) in the detail. Kept as printed.
